description:
Our PADI Divemaster Program in Honolulu, Hawaiʻi is designed to transform experienced divers into confident dive professionals. You’ll gain the knowledge, skills, and leadership abilities to work anywhere in the world as a PADI Pro.

 [PADI Blog: How to Become a Divemaster](https://blog.padi.com/new-year-new-career-becoming-a-padi-divemaster/)
what_is_included:
- PADI Divemaster eLearning + Digital Crew-Pak (includes slates & pro bag) ($543 Dollar Value)

- Confined-water training blocks scheduled as needed (waterskills, equipment exchange, skill-circuit practice)

- Ocean training days (primarily two-tank boat charters) aligned to course requirements and conditions

- Tanks, weights, and air fills for all training dives

- 24-skill demonstration-quality circuit with video feedback and coaching

- Waterskills assessments & coaching: 400 m swim, 15-min tread, 800 m snorkel, 100 m tow, equipment exchange

- Practical Skills workshops: dive-site setup & management, professional dive briefing, search & recovery (knots/patterns/lift bag), deep-dive scenario (DSMB deploy), dive-site mapping project

- Divemaster-Conducted Program workshops: ReActivate, Discover Local Diving, Discover Scuba Diving (confined & OW), and Skin Diver/Snorkeling supervision

- Real-world leadership days: assist with actual student classes and guide certified divers under supervision

- Emergency Assistance Plan (EAP) project for a local dive site

- Weekly 1:1 mentor check-ins + career coaching

- Use of specialized training gear during workshops (DSMB/spool, lift bag, lines, knot kits)

- All boat briefings, site orientations, and post-dive debriefs included

- Course administration, training records, and certification application support (PADI application fees paid to PADI separately)
what_is_not_included:
- PADI Divemaster application/processing fee — paid directly to PADI (currently $162)

- Personal scuba equipment — full kit (mask/snorkel/fins/boots, wetsuit, regulator, BCD, computer, DSMB & spool, cutting tool, compass, light)

- Rental bundle (full program): $210 total

- Professional liability insurance (post-certification, if guiding/working as a pro)

- Medical exam/doctor’s clearance

- EFR/CPR course or renewal (if not current within 24 months)

- Enriched Air/Nitrox upgrades and nitrox fills (optional)

- Extra training days/makeup sessions/extra boat spots beyond the standard curriculum

- Travel & accommodation

- Marina parking: $1 per hour (pay at meter; marina rules apply)

- Optional specialty courses not listed under “Included”

- PADI professional membership dues (annual, after certification)

- Dive accident insurance (e.g., DAN) — recommended but not included
itinerary:
**This is a sample schedule; your exact plan will be set during a one-on-one with the Course Director.**

Pre-course: eLearning access & onboarding 

- Week 1: Orientation • Confined-water training block (waterskills & skill-circuit practice) • Ocean training day • Knowledge sessions • EAP & Mapping project briefing

- Week 2: Confined-water block (equipment exchange + demo-quality polish) • Ocean training days • Workshops: ReActivate & DSD (confined) • Skill-circuit video review • Mentor check-in

- Week 3: Leadership days assisting real classes (confined & open water) • Search & Recovery workshop (knots/patterns/lift) • Deep-dive scenario (DSMB deploy) • Workshop: DLD guided dive

- Week 4: Practical Assessments (OWD confined/OW, Continue-Ed, Certified-diver guiding) • Map & EAP finalize • Knowledge reviews & final exams • Admin & next-steps coaching

**Notes**

Built-in flex days for weather, boat/shore mix, and remediation as needed.

Session count, boat/shore balance, and leadership rotations vary by progress, conditions, and availability.

special_requirements:
#Divemaster Course prerequisites:

• Advanced Open Water & Rescue Diver certification
• 40 logged dives to begin (60 required for certification)
• EFR (CPR/First Aid) within 24 months
• Medical clearance within 12 months
• Minimum age: 18 years

faqs:
#What is a PADI Pro?
First, it’s important to understand the differences between recreational diving and professional diving. Recreational divers dive for the adventure and underwater exploration. Professional divers love these things, too, but they are also specially trained to teach and guide others in their underwater adventures.

#How Do I Become a PADI Pro?
To become a PADI Pro, you must first complete the PADI Divemaster course which will hone your scuba diving skills and prepare you to assist scuba instructors and supervise diving activities. Next, you can go on to become a PADI Open Water Scuba Instructor (OWSI), to build on your Divemaster knowledge and develop your teaching skills. An OWSI can teach all of the core PADI courses up to the Divemaster rating. OWSI’s can also earn PADI Specialty Instructor ratings, such as Wreck Diving Instructor, to expand their course offerings.

A PADI Pro is someone who has extensively developed their underwater skills, leadership abilities, teaching abilities, and role of responsibility among the diving community. Undertaking a PADI Professional course is the crucial step in crafting a successful career in diving!

#Is PADI a Professional Certification?
PADI offers both recreational and professional dive certifications, with over 30,000,000 divers and counting. PADI professional scuba certifications are globally recognized; you can travel the world and do what you love or share your dive knowledge locally. As a PADI Divemaster or PADI Instructor, you’ll learn how to lead scuba dives and help others with their dive education.

#What’s the Difference Between a PADI Master Scuba Diver, Divemaster, and Instructor?
Let’s start with Master Scuba Diver, as this is the odd one out here. This is not a professional level certification, but a recognition that you’ve done enough specialty courses at a recreational level to demonstrate that you are an experience diver who really cares about your training. Although Master Scuba Diver is an elite level to reach, achieving this is not the same as being qualified to teach scuba diving.

Next, we have Divemaster, which is the first of the PADI professional qualifications. If you’re looking to become an Instructor, this is the first step you will need to take. PADI Divemasters are not qualified to teach, however, they are qualified to act as dive guides, and to assist Instructors – you can read more about this further down the page.

A PADI Instructor is fully qualified to teach scuba diving, at a range of levels. For example, a PADI open water instructor may have taught your Open Water course, Advanced Open Water course, Rescue Diver course, or any number of specialty courses. 

[PADI Pro FAQ Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0i-HKwhxUd8)
